A checklist of the mistakes that most often make a chart mislead or confuse, as **70 flash cards** in
8 groups. Read the title, decide what the problem is and how you would fix it, then **open the card**.
Use **Practise** to be dealt the cards one at a time; the ones you mark *Review again* come back first.

Most of these points are taught in [Best Practices](best_practices.qmd), [Matching Data to Plots](plot_data.qmd)
and the ggplot2 modules; each card links to where. The list of topics follows the caveats collection of
[data-to-viz.com](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveats.html) by Yan Holtz and Conor Healy, where many cards have a
longer illustrated page (the "data-to-viz" link on the card). The wording and the R code here are our own.

## Misleading charts {.cv-heading data-cat="Misleading charts"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Misleading charts"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Do not cut the y-axis of a bar chart</summary>

**Problem.** Bars encode values by their length. Starting the axis at 120 mmHg makes a 3 mmHg gap look like a doubling.

**Fix.** Start bar charts at zero. If the differences matter but are small, show points with confidence intervals instead of bars.

```r
ggplot(d, aes(group, sbp)) + geom_col() + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA))
```

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/cut_y_axis.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Box plots hide the shape</summary>

**Problem.** Two groups can have identical boxes while one is bimodal and the other is not; small groups look as solid as large ones.

**Fix.** Add the raw points (jittered), or use a violin or raincloud, and print the n per group.

```r
geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4)
```

[In the course: Merged Visuals](../specialized/merge_visuals.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/boxplot.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Avoid counter-intuitive encodings</summary>

**Problem.** Readers expect up = more, red = bad, bigger = larger. An inverted axis or a reversed colour scale makes them read the opposite of the truth.

**Fix.** Keep the usual direction; if you must invert (e.g. ranks), say so on the axis and in the title.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/counter_intuitive.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Bars with error bars ("dynamite plots") hide the data</summary>

**Problem.** A bar of the mean with an error bar shows two numbers and suggests values below the mean are the only ones that exist.

**Fix.** Show the individual points with the mean and its 95% CI, or a box/violin plot. State whether bars are SD, SE or CI.

```r
stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = 'pointrange') + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.3)
```

[In the course: Statistical Plots](../specialized/plot_stats.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/error_bar.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Be wary of two y-axes</summary>

**Problem.** The scales of the two axes are arbitrary, so any two series can be made to cross, diverge or move together.

**Fix.** Use two panels with a shared x-axis, or index both series to 100 at the start.

```r
facet_wrap(~ series, ncol = 1, scales = 'free_y')
```

[In the course: Matching Data to Plots](../data-visualization/plot_data.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/dual_axis.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Avoid 3D</summary>

**Problem.** Perspective makes nearer bars and slices look bigger and hides some values behind others.

**Fix.** Use the 2D version. Three numeric variables? Colour or size for the third, or small multiples.

[In the course: Matching Data to Plots](../data-visualization/plot_data.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/3d.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Do not cherry-pick the data</summary>

**Problem.** Choosing the start date, the sites or the subgroup that tells the best story misleads even when every point is correct.

**Fix.** Show the full period and all groups, and say why any are left out.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Draw proportions accurately</summary>

**Problem.** Icons or shapes scaled by height and width (both) exaggerate differences; a doubled value looks four times larger.

**Fix.** Make area (not radius or height and width together) proportional to the value, or simply use bars.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Respect time intervals</summary>

**Problem.** Unevenly spaced dates (2010, 2015, 2020, 2021, 2022) drawn at equal distances distort the trend.

**Fix.** Use a real date or numeric x-axis so the gaps are drawn to scale.

```r
aes(x = as.Date(visit_date))   # not factor(visit_date)
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Show the sample size</summary>

**Problem.** A percentage from 8 people looks as solid as one from 800.

**Fix.** Print the n on the axis labels, in the legend or in a caption; add confidence intervals.

```r
scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) paste0(x, '\n(n = ', table(d$group)[x], ')'))
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Misleading charts"}
<details>
<summary>Beware of Simpson's paradox</summary>

**Problem.** A trend in the pooled data can reverse inside every subgroup when the groups differ in size and level.

**Fix.** Colour or facet by the likely confounder before drawing a conclusion; adjust for it in the model.

```r
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, colour = group)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = 'lm')
```

[In the course: Regression Analysis](../statistical-analysis/regression.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/simpson.html) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Wrong chart type {.cv-heading data-cat="Wrong chart type"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Wrong chart type"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>Many thin lollipops or bars can shimmer</summary>

**Problem.** Dozens of closely spaced thin lines create a moiré pattern that is tiring to look at.

**Fix.** Use fewer, thicker bars, or a dot plot, or aggregate into groups.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>The trouble with pie charts</summary>

**Problem.** People compare angles and areas poorly; slices of 23% and 27% look the same, and more than 5 slices are unreadable.

**Fix.** A sorted bar chart. Keep a pie only for 2–3 parts of a whole for a general audience.

```r
ggplot(d, aes(reorder(cause, n), n)) + geom_col() + coord_flip()
```

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/pie.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>Radial bars distort length</summary>

**Problem.** In a circular bar chart the outer bars are longer than inner bars of the same value.

**Fix.** Use straight bars; keep radial layouts for a decorative overview with labels on the values.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/circular_barplot_accordeon.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>Maybe you do not need a map</summary>

**Problem.** A map draws attention to large, empty areas; if geography is not the question, it wastes space.

**Fix.** A sorted bar or dot chart of the regions answers "which is highest?" better than a map.

[In the course: Maps and Choropleths](../gis/maps_choropleth.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>Two values per group? Try a dumbbell</summary>

**Problem.** Grouped bars for before/after (or men/women) make the reader compare bars across pairs.

**Fix.** A dumbbell (two points joined by a line) shows both values and the change in one glance.

```r
geom_segment(aes(x = before, xend = after, y = site, yend = site)) + geom_point(aes(before, site)) + geom_point(aes(after, site))
```

[In the course: Showcase](../plot-gallery/showcase.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Wrong chart type"}
<details>
<summary>Use circular bar plots with care</summary>

**Problem.** Without a radial axis readers cannot read values, and the shape is driven by the order of the bars.

**Fix.** Label each bar with its value and sort it; prefer a straight bar chart for comparison.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/circular_bar_yaxis.html) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Colour {.cv-heading data-cat="Colour"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Colour"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Use colour on purpose</summary>

**Problem.** Colouring every bar differently adds a legend and implies groups that mean nothing.

**Fix.** One colour by default; add colour only to encode a variable or to highlight the message (grey + one accent).

```r
geom_col(aes(fill = site == 'Hospital B')) + scale_fill_manual(values = c('grey70', '#C0392B'), guide = 'none')
```

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/color_com_nothing.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Choose the background on purpose</summary>

**Problem.** A dark or coloured panel background reduces contrast and changes how colours look.

**Fix.** White or very light grey backgrounds; theme_minimal() or theme_classic().

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Keep enough contrast</summary>

**Problem.** Light-yellow lines or pale text on white disappear on a projector and in print.

**Fix.** Check contrast (text should be dark); avoid the lightest end of a palette for thin lines and text.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Avoid pure, saturated colours</summary>

**Problem.** Pure red, green and blue (#FF0000 ...) vibrate next to each other and tire the eye.

**Fix.** Muted palettes (viridis, ColorBrewer, Okabe-Ito) with one stronger colour for emphasis.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Numbers need a sequential palette</summary>

**Problem.** A rainbow or qualitative palette on a numeric variable has no visual order.

**Fix.** One hue from light to dark (or viridis) so darker = more.

```r
scale_fill_viridis_c()   # or scale_fill_distiller(palette = 'Blues', direction = 1)
```

[In the course: ggplot2 Module 3](../data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_3_colors_scales_themes.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Too many colours kill the story</summary>

**Problem.** Beyond about 6 colours readers cannot match lines to the legend.

**Fix.** Highlight 1–3 groups and grey the rest, or use small multiples.

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>No gradient for unordered groups</summary>

**Problem.** A light-to-dark gradient on regions or treatments suggests an order that does not exist.

**Fix.** A qualitative palette (scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set2') or Okabe-Ito) for categories.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Avoid the rainbow palette</summary>

**Problem.** Rainbow scales have sudden bright bands (yellow, cyan) that create boundaries not in the data, and fail in greyscale.

**Fix.** viridis or a single-hue sequential scale.

[data-to-viz](https://blog.datawrapper.de/colors/) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Diverging data, diverging palette</summary>

**Problem.** Change from baseline, residuals and correlations have a meaningful zero that a sequential palette hides.

**Fix.** Two hues meeting at a neutral colour placed exactly at the midpoint.

```r
scale_fill_gradient2(low = '#2166AC', mid = 'white', high = '#B2182B', midpoint = 0)
```

[In the course: ggplot2 Module 3](../data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_3_colors_scales_themes.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Colour"}
<details>
<summary>Think of colour-blind readers</summary>

**Problem.** About 1 in 12 men cannot tell red from green.

**Fix.** Colour-blind-safe palettes (viridis, Okabe-Ito), plus redundant cues (shape, direct labels).

```r
scale_colour_viridis_d()
```

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Design {.cv-heading data-cat="Design"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Design"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Align everything with something</summary>

**Problem.** Titles, panels and annotations that float at random positions look messy and hard to scan.

**Fix.** Left-align title, subtitle and caption with the plot; use the same margins across panels.

```r
theme(plot.title.position = 'plot', plot.caption.position = 'plot')
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Two fonts are enough</summary>

**Problem.** Many fonts and styles compete for attention.

**Fix.** One font family; vary size and weight for hierarchy.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Do you need that box?</summary>

**Problem.** Borders around the panel, legend and plot add ink without information.

**Fix.** Remove panel borders and legend boxes; let white space separate elements.

```r
theme(panel.border = element_blank(), legend.background = element_blank())
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Font size matters</summary>

**Problem.** Default 11 pt axis text is unreadable on a slide or a printed half-page.

**Fix.** Set base_size for the output (about 14–18 for slides); check the figure at its final size.

```r
theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Group what belongs together</summary>

**Problem.** Related bars or panels far apart force the eye to jump.

**Fix.** Order categories so comparisons are adjacent; group panels by the question they answer.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Make the title say something</summary>

**Problem.** A title like "SBP by group" makes the reader find the message themselves.

**Fix.** State the finding in the title ("SBP fell by 9 mmHg with the intervention") and keep the description in the subtitle.

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Design"}
<details>
<summary>Declutter</summary>

**Problem.** Heavy grids, tick marks, borders and legends compete with the data.

**Fix.** Light or no grid lines, direct labels instead of legends, no redundant text.

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/declutter.html) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Maps {.cv-heading data-cat="Maps"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Maps"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Maps"}
<details>
<summary>Do not move regions around</summary>

**Problem.** Moving or resizing islands and remote areas to fit the frame changes their apparent size and position.

**Fix.** If you must inset a region, frame it and say so; keep the same projection.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Maps"}
<details>
<summary>Mind the projection</summary>

**Problem.** Web Mercator inflates areas far from the equator, so a choropleth over-weights them.

**Fix.** Use an equal-area or local projected CRS for thematic maps (e.g. UTM for a district).

```r
st_transform(blocks, 32644)
```

[In the course: Spatial Data with sf](../gis/spatial_data_sf.qmd) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Maps"}
<details>
<summary>Normalise your maps</summary>

**Problem.** A map of counts is mostly a map of where people live.

**Fix.** Map rates (per 100,000) or ratios to expected; show counts only when workload is the question.

```r
mutate(rate = cases / population * 1e5)
```

[In the course: Maps and Choropleths](../gis/maps_choropleth.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://xkcd.com/1138/) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Maps"}
<details>
<summary>Show missing data as missing</summary>

**Problem.** A missing area coloured like the lowest class looks like "no disease".

**Fix.** Give missing areas a distinct neutral colour or hatching and a legend entry.

```r
scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = 'grey85')
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Maps"}
<details>
<summary>Do not let small regions vanish</summary>

**Problem.** Dense urban wards are tiny on a map, though they hold most people.

**Fix.** Add an inset or zoom, a cartogram, or a hexagon tile map.

[In the course: Geographic Advanced](../plot-gallery/advanced/3.6_geographic_advanced.qmd) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Labels and legends {.cv-heading data-cat="Labels and legends"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Labels and legends"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Prefer horizontal labels</summary>

**Problem.** Rotated axis labels are hard to read.

**Fix.** Flip the axes so long category names sit horizontally.

```r
ggplot(d, aes(n, reorder(diagnosis, n))) + geom_col()
```

[In the course: Best Practices](../data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/hard_label.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Use legends sparingly</summary>

**Problem.** A legend makes the eye jump back and forth.

**Fix.** Label lines and groups directly at their ends; drop the legend.

```r
geom_text(data = last_points, aes(label = group), hjust = 0) + theme(legend.position = 'none')
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Do not put labels on top of the data</summary>

**Problem.** Text over points or lines hides what it describes.

**Fix.** Offset labels, use ggrepel, or place them in empty space.

```r
ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = name))
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Round your numbers</summary>

**Problem.** A value like "37.4285%" suggests a precision the data do not have and is harder to read.

**Fix.** Round to what matters (37%); use scales::percent() for axes.

```r
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Annotation is crucial</summary>

**Problem.** Readers miss the event or threshold that explains the pattern.

**Fix.** Add a short note, a reference line or a shaded period where it matters.

```r
geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date('2024-06-01'), linetype = 2) + annotate('text', ...)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/annotation.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Labels and legends"}
<details>
<summary>Do not label every tick</summary>

**Problem.** A label on every year or category crowds the axis.

**Fix.** Fewer, round breaks.

```r
scale_x_date(date_breaks = '6 months', date_labels = '%b %Y')
```

</details>
:::

:::

## Dashboards and data stories {.cv-heading data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}
<details>
<summary>Keep colours consistent across charts</summary>

**Problem.** If "Intervention" is blue in one panel and orange in the next, readers mis-match them.

**Fix.** A named colour vector used by every plot.

```r
arm_cols <- c(Control = 'grey50', Intervention = '#2C5F8D'); scale_colour_manual(values = arm_cols)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/consistency.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}
<details>
<summary>Share the y-axis to compare panels</summary>

**Problem.** Panels with their own y range look similar even when one is ten times higher.

**Fix.** Keep scales fixed when the panels are compared (the facet default); free them only to show shape.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}
<details>
<summary>Leave margins between charts</summary>

**Problem.** Panels pressed together read as one figure.

**Fix.** Space and alignment between panels (patchwork handles both).

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Dashboards and data stories"}
<details>
<summary>Link charts that share an axis</summary>

**Problem.** Separate charts with the same x (time) are hard to read together.

**Fix.** Stack them vertically with aligned x-axes, or link them interactively (crosstalk).

[In the course: Interactive Plots](../specialized/interactive.qmd) 

</details>
:::

:::

## Other {.cv-heading data-cat="Other"}

::: {.cv-grid data-cat="Other"}

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Sort your bar chart</summary>

**Problem.** Alphabetical order hides the ranking.

**Fix.** Order bars by value (unless the categories have their own order, like age groups).

```r
aes(x = reorder(region, rate))   # or forcats::fct_reorder()
```

[In the course: Basic Plot Gallery](../plot-gallery/basic.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/order_data.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Histograms - mind the bin width</summary>

**Problem.** The same data can look smooth, bimodal or noisy depending on the bins.

**Fix.** Try several widths and choose a meaningful one (5 mmHg, 1 year); report it.

```r
geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/bin_size.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Size bubbles by area, not radius</summary>

**Problem.** If the radius doubles, the area quadruples.

**Fix.** ggplot2's scale_size() already maps to area; avoid scale_radius().

```r
scale_size_area(max_size = 12)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/radius_or_area.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>The spaghetti plot</summary>

**Problem.** Twenty overlapping lines are unreadable.

**Fix.** Grey all lines and highlight one or a few, or small multiples with the others in grey behind.

[In the course: Showcase](../plot-gallery/showcase.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/spaghetti.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Connect only connected dots</summary>

**Problem.** A line implies continuity between points; joining unrelated categories invents a trend.

**Fix.** Lines for ordered x (time, dose); points or bars for categories.

[In the course: ggplot2 Module 1](../data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_1_foundations_geoms.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/connect_your_dot.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Drawing order matters</summary>

**Problem.** The layer drawn last hides the others: a large group can bury a small one.

**Fix.** Draw the highlight last; use transparency.

```r
geom_point(data = others, colour = 'grey') + geom_point(data = highlight, colour = 'red')
```

[In the course: ggplot2 Module 4](../data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_4_advanced_best_practices.qmd) 

</details>

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Overlapping sets? Use an UpSet plot</summary>

**Problem.** Venn diagrams with more than three sets (e.g. comorbidities) are unreadable.

**Fix.** An UpSet plot shows the size of every intersection as a bar.

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Stacked charts are hard to read</summary>

**Problem.** Only the bottom segment has a common baseline; the rest cannot be compared.

**Fix.** Grouped bars, small multiples, or 100% stacks with few segments.

[In the course: Matching Data to Plots](../data-visualization/plot_data.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/stacking.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Mind the aspect ratio</summary>

**Problem.** Stretching a plot changes how steep a trend looks.

**Fix.** Choose the width/height on purpose (about 45° for the main slopes); set it in ggsave().

```r
ggsave('fig.png', width = 7, height = 4)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/aspect_ratio.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Make date axes easy to read</summary>

**Problem.** Default date labels can be dense or ambiguous (01/02).

**Fix.** Unambiguous formats ("Jan 2025") and sensible breaks.

```r
scale_x_date(date_labels = '%b %Y')
```

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Reorder your heat map</summary>

**Problem.** Rows and columns in input order hide any structure.

**Fix.** Order by a summary or by clustering so similar rows sit together.

```r
aes(y = fct_reorder(ward, cases, .fun = sum))
```

[In the course: Showcase](../plot-gallery/showcase.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/graph/heatmap.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Beware of overplotting</summary>

**Problem.** With thousands of points the scatter becomes a solid blob.

**Fix.** Transparency, smaller points, hexbins or 2D density.

```r
geom_point(alpha = 0.2)   # or geom_hex()
```

[In the course: Intermediate Plot Gallery](../plot-gallery/moderate.qmd) · [data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/overplotting.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Too many distributions at once</summary>

**Problem.** Overlaid densities or histograms for many groups become a tangle.

**Fix.** A ridgeline plot, small multiples or box plots side by side.

```r
ggridges::geom_density_ridges()
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/multi_distribution.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Small multiples - rows or columns?</summary>

**Problem.** The layout decides what is easy to compare: aligned y values compare across a row, aligned x values down a column.

**Fix.** Put panels in one row to compare heights, in one column to compare positions on x.

```r
facet_wrap(~ group, nrow = 1)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/small_multiple.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Check the numbers on the chart</summary>

**Problem.** Percentages that do not add to 100, or totals that do not match the table, destroy trust.

**Fix.** Compute labels from the data in code; never type them by hand.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/calculation_error.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Do not make readers do arithmetic</summary>

**Problem.** If the message is a difference, two lines make the reader subtract in their head.

**Fix.** Plot the difference itself (with its CI).

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/mental_calculation.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Area is a weak encoding</summary>

**Problem.** People underestimate area differences; bubbles and treemaps give rough impressions only.

**Fix.** Use position or length when exact comparison matters.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/area_hard.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Grouped bars must look grouped</summary>

**Problem.** Evenly spaced bars hide which belong together.

**Fix.** Dodge within a group and leave a gap between groups.

```r
geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7)
```

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/grouped_bar.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Radar (spider) charts mislead</summary>

**Problem.** The area depends on the order of the axes, and values are hard to read.

**Fix.** A dot plot or parallel coordinates for several measures per item.

[data-to-viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/spider.html) 

</details>
:::

::: {.cv-card data-cat="Other"}
<details>
<summary>Log scales for rates of change</summary>

**Problem.** On a linear axis exponential growth looks explosive and early changes look flat.

**Fix.** A log axis when relative change is the question; label it clearly.

```r
scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma)
```

</details>
:::

<details>
<summary>It is "choropleth"</summary>

**Problem.** The common misspelling "chloropleth" undermines a report.

**Fix.** choro (area) + pleth (quantity).

<script>
/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 * quiz.js — tiny self-check quiz engine for reveal.js / any HTML page
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Vanilla JS, zero dependencies, works offline (file://) and inside
 * Quarto reveal.js decks with embed-resources.
 *
 * SYNTAX (what lives in the .qmd — a Pandoc fenced div with data-attrs)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
 *   MCQ (single answer)
 *   ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="<hash>"
 *         data-show="<base64>" data-explain="<base64>"}
 *   Which model suits a binary outcome?
 *
 *   - Linear regression
 *   - Logistic regression
 *   - Cox regression
 *   :::
 *
 *   Fill-in-the-blank
 *   ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q4" data-type="fill" data-hashes="<h1>,<h2>"
 *         data-show="<base64>" data-explain="<base64>"}
 *   Which gtsummary function builds Table 1?
 *   :::
 *
 *   data-qid      unique id (it salts the hashes)
 *   data-hash     hash of the correct option INDEX (0-based) — mcq
 *   data-hashes   comma-separated hashes of each accepted answer — fill
 *   data-show     base64 of the text revealed by "Show answer"
 *   data-explain  base64 of the short explanation (basic `code` allowed)
 *
 * You never write those attributes by hand. Use the R helpers in
 * assets/quiz.R, which take PLAIN text and emit the fenced div:
 *
 *   ```{r}
 *   #| echo: false
 *   #| output: asis
 *   source("assets/quiz.R")
 *   quiz_mcq("s1q1", "Which model suits a binary outcome?",
 *            c("Linear", "Logistic", "Cox"), answer = 2,
 *            explain = "Binary outcome -> logit link -> logistic.")
 *   quiz_fill("s1q4", "Which gtsummary function builds Table 1?",
 *             accept = c("tbl_summary", "tbl_summary()"),
 *             explain = "tbl_summary() summarises variables, optionally by a group.")
 *   ```
 *
 * Optional: <span class="quiz-score"></span> anywhere shows "x / y", followed by
 *   "Save score" (downloads a text file) and "Reset" buttons. The first-attempt
 *   results are kept in localStorage per deck, so a reload keeps the score.
 *
 * BEHAVIOUR
 *   - MCQ: options are SHUFFLED at load (hash uses the authored index, so
 *     data-hash is unaffected; add data-shuffle="0" to keep authored order).
 *     Click an option -> instant ✔/✘; explanation appears after the
 *     attempt (or after "Show answer").
 *   - Fill: type + Enter / "Check". Answers are normalised (case,
 *     surrounding/duplicate whitespace, backticks, trailing "()") before
 *     hashing, so "  TBL_Summary() " matches "tbl_summary".
 *   - Answers are NOT in the page source: only salted hashes are, and the
 *     explanation / reveal text is base64-encoded. This stops casual
 *     view-source peeking; it is NOT cryptographic security.
 *
 * HASH (must match quiz.R exactly): two polynomial rolling hashes over
 *   the string  qid + "|" + value , base-36 encoded and concatenated.
 * ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var M1 = 2147483629, M2 = 2147483587;

  function hash(str) {
    var a = 5381, b = 52711;
    for (var i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      var c = str.charCodeAt(i);
      a = (a * 131 + c) % M1;
      b = (b * 137 + c) % M2;
    }
    return a.toString(36) + '.' + b.toString(36);
  }

  function normalise(s) {
    return String(s).toLowerCase()
      .replace(/`/g, '')
      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
      .trim()
      .replace(/\(\s*\)$/, '')   // "tbl_summary()" == "tbl_summary"
      .trim();
  }

  function b64(s) {
    if (!s) return '';
    try {
      var bin = atob(s), bytes = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
      for (var i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) bytes[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
      return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes);
    } catch (e) { return ''; }
  }

  function esc(s) {
    return s.replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>');
  }
  // escape first, then allow `code` only
  function lite(s) { return esc(s).replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, '<code>$1</code>'); }

  var state = { total: 0, correct: 0, scored: {} };

  // ── saved score ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The first-attempt result of each question is kept in the browser
  // (localStorage, one entry per deck file), so a reload keeps the score.
  // "Save score" downloads a small text file a participant can keep or
  // hand in; "Reset" clears the saved result for this deck.
  var deckName = (location.pathname.split('/').pop() || 'deck').replace(/\.html?$/, '');
  // Kept per workshop folder and deck: deck file names repeat across workshops
  // (s5_choose_check_report is in three). Older versions used the deck name alone; that copy
  // is read once, for this deck's questions only, so no saved score is lost.
  var folder = location.pathname.split('/').slice(-2, -1)[0] || '';
  var STORE = 'quiz-score:' + (folder ? folder + '/' : '') + deckName;
  var LEGACY = 'quiz-score:' + deckName;
  function persist() { try { localStorage.setItem(STORE, JSON.stringify(state.scored)); } catch (e) {} }
  function restore() {
    try {
      var saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORE));
      var migrate = !saved && STORE !== LEGACY;
      if (!saved) saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LEGACY)) || {};
      var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
      for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
        var id = qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid');
        if (saved.hasOwnProperty(id)) { state.scored[id] = !!saved[id]; if (saved[id]) state.correct++; }
      }
      if (migrate && Object.keys(state.scored).length) persist();
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  // Reset: forget this deck's answers, also in the old shared copy (other decks keep theirs there).
  function forget() {
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem(STORE);
      var old = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LEGACY));
      if (old && STORE !== LEGACY) {
        var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
        for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) delete old[qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid')];
        if (Object.keys(old).length) localStorage.setItem(LEGACY, JSON.stringify(old)); else localStorage.removeItem(LEGACY);
      }
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  function scoreText() {
    var lines = ['Quiz score', 'Deck: ' + (document.title || deckName), 'File: ' + deckName, 'Saved: ' + new Date().toLocaleString(),
                 'Score (first attempt): ' + state.correct + ' / ' + state.total, ''];
    var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
    for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
      var id = qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid');
      lines.push(id + ': ' + (state.scored.hasOwnProperty(id) ? (state.scored[id] ? 'correct' : 'not correct') : 'not attempted'));
    }
    return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
  }
  function download() {
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = 'data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,' + encodeURIComponent(scoreText());
    a.download = 'quiz_' + deckName + '.txt';
    document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove();
  }
  function addScoreTools() {
    var els = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-score');
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      if (els[i].getAttribute('data-tools')) continue;
      els[i].setAttribute('data-tools', '1');
      var box = document.createElement('span'); box.className = 'quiz-score-tools';
      var sv = document.createElement('button'); sv.type = 'button'; sv.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost quiz-save'; sv.textContent = 'Save score';
      sv.addEventListener('click', download);
      var rs = document.createElement('button'); rs.type = 'button'; rs.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost quiz-reset'; rs.textContent = 'Reset';
      rs.addEventListener('click', function () { forget(); location.reload(); });
      box.appendChild(sv); box.appendChild(rs);
      els[i].parentNode.insertBefore(box, els[i].nextSibling);
    }
  }

  function updateScores() {
    var els = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-score');
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      els[i].textContent = state.correct + ' / ' + state.total;
    }
  }

  function record(qid, ok) {
    if (state.scored.hasOwnProperty(qid)) return;      // first attempt only
    state.scored[qid] = !!ok;
    if (ok) state.correct++;
    persist();
    updateScores();
  }

  function feedback(q, ok, msg) {
    var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
    fb.className = 'quiz-feedback ' + (ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
    fb.innerHTML = (ok ? '✔ Correct. ' : '✘ Not quite. ') + (msg ? lite(msg) : '');
  }

  function explanation(q) {
    var ex = b64(q.getAttribute('data-explain'));
    return ex;
  }

  function buildCommon(q) {
    var fb = document.createElement('div');
    fb.className = 'quiz-feedback';
    fb.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
    q.appendChild(fb);

    var show = document.createElement('button');
    show.type = 'button';
    show.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost';
    show.textContent = 'Show answer';
    q.appendChild(show);
    return { fb: fb, show: show };
  }

  function initMCQ(q) {
    var qid = q.getAttribute('data-qid');
    var correctHash = q.getAttribute('data-hash');
    var list = q.querySelector('ul, ol');
    if (!list) return;
    // authored index is what the hash is built on; DISPLAY order is shuffled so the
    // answer position (and any length/position tell) cannot be learned.
    var items = Array.prototype.slice.call(list.children).map(function (li, i) { return { li: li, i: i }; });
    if (q.getAttribute('data-shuffle') !== '0') {
      for (var k = items.length - 1; k > 0; k--) {
        var r = Math.floor(Math.random() * (k + 1)), t = items[k]; items[k] = items[r]; items[r] = t;
      }
    }
    var wrap = document.createElement('div');
    wrap.className = 'quiz-options';
    var btns = items.map(function (it, pos) {
      var b = document.createElement('button');
      b.type = 'button';
      b.className = 'quiz-option';
      b.setAttribute('data-i', it.i);
      b.innerHTML = '<span class="quiz-letter">' + String.fromCharCode(65 + pos) + '</span>' + it.li.innerHTML;
      wrap.appendChild(b);
      return b;
    });
    list.parentNode.replaceChild(wrap, list);
    var c = buildCommon(q);

    function isCorrect(i) { return hash(qid + '|' + i) === correctHash; }
    function orig(b) { return parseInt(b.getAttribute('data-i'), 10); }
    function reveal() {
      btns.forEach(function (b) { if (isCorrect(orig(b))) b.classList.add('is-correct'); });
    }

    btns.forEach(function (b) {
      b.addEventListener('click', function () {
        var ok = isCorrect(orig(b));
        b.classList.add(ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
        record(qid, ok);
        feedback(q, ok, explanation(q));
        if (ok) btns.forEach(function (x) { x.disabled = true; });
      });
    });
    c.show.addEventListener('click', function () {
      reveal();
      record(qid, false);
      var ans = b64(q.getAttribute('data-show'));
      var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
      fb.className = 'quiz-feedback is-info';
      fb.innerHTML = 'Answer: <strong>' + lite(ans) + '</strong>. ' + lite(explanation(q));
      btns.forEach(function (x) { x.disabled = true; });
    });
  }

  function initFill(q) {
    var qid = q.getAttribute('data-qid');
    var accepted = (q.getAttribute('data-hashes') || '').split(',');
    var row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'quiz-fill';
    var input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.className = 'quiz-input';
    input.placeholder = 'type your answer…';
    input.setAttribute('autocomplete', 'off');
    input.setAttribute('autocapitalize', 'off');
    input.setAttribute('spellcheck', 'false');
    var check = document.createElement('button');
    check.type = 'button';
    check.className = 'quiz-btn';
    check.textContent = 'Check';
    row.appendChild(input);
    row.appendChild(check);
    q.appendChild(row);
    var c = buildCommon(q);

    function submit() {
      var v = normalise(input.value);
      if (!v) return;
      var ok = accepted.indexOf(hash(qid + '|' + v)) !== -1;
      input.classList.remove('is-correct', 'is-wrong');
      input.classList.add(ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
      record(qid, ok);
      feedback(q, ok, explanation(q));
    }
    check.addEventListener('click', submit);
    // keep reveal.js shortcuts (space, arrows, f, s, …) out of the text box
    ['keydown', 'keyup', 'keypress'].forEach(function (ev) {
      input.addEventListener(ev, function (e) {
        e.stopPropagation();
        if (ev === 'keydown' && e.key === 'Enter') submit();
      });
    });
    c.show.addEventListener('click', function () {
      record(qid, false);
      var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
      fb.className = 'quiz-feedback is-info';
      fb.innerHTML = 'Answer: <strong>' + lite(b64(q.getAttribute('data-show'))) + '</strong>. ' + lite(explanation(q));
    });
  }

  function init() {
    var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
    state.total = qs.length;
    for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
      var q = qs[i];
      if (q.getAttribute('data-quiz-ready')) continue;
      q.setAttribute('data-quiz-ready', '1');
      var type = q.getAttribute('data-type');
      if (type === 'mcq') initMCQ(q);
      else if (type === 'fill') initFill(q);
    }
    restore();
    addScoreTools();
    updateScores();
  }

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
  else init();

  // exposed for tests / tooling
  window.Quiz = { hash: hash, normalise: normalise };
})();
</script>
